 Judgment

Claimants are before this Court assailing the judgment and award dated 01.03.2016 passed in LACA No.128/2016 by the I Additional District Judge, Kalaburagi (for short 'Appellate Court') enhancing compensation to Rs.2,29,248/- per acre for dry land, modifying the judgment and award dated 28.09.2012 passed in LAC No.18/2009 by the Senior Civil Judge, Kalaburagi (for short 'Reference Court'), the appellants are seeking for further enhancement.

2. Heard Sri Harshavardhan .R. Malipatil, learned counsel appearing for the claimants/appellants,
Smt Archana P. Tiwari, learned Additional Advocate General along with Sri F. M. Inamdar, High Court Government Pleader for the respondents.
3.

Land bearing Sy.No.37/1 measuring 20 guntas, Sy.No.37/2 measuring 8 guntas and Sy.No.37/3 measuring 7 guntas totally measuring 1 acre 2 guntas of Bommanhalli (Vaijapur village) Taluka Aland, District NC: 2024:KHC-K:4669 Kalaburagi, was acquired by the respondent under 4(1)
notification dated 28.06.2007 for the purpose of construction of Irrigation Tank.

The Land Acquisition Officer awarded compensation of Rs.37,500/- per acre for dry land; in the reference sought before the Reference Court, the compensation was enhanced to Rs.1,48,000/- per acre and in the appeal preferred by the claimants before the Appellate Court compensation of Rs.2,29,248/-
has been awarded.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants, taking this Court to Ex.P4 - consent award in another acquisition proceedings, submits that for similarly situated lands as in the acquired lands, the compensation of Rs.9,00,000/- per acre has been awarded, according to the learned counsel, Ex.
P4 - the consent award is to be considered and applying the escalation of 5% per annum, the market value could be worked out in an appropriate manner

. It is submitted that the potentiality of the land acquired in the instant case and the lands acquired under Ex.P4-consent NC: 2024:KHC-K:4669 award are exemplars, as is evident from Ex.P4 and the preliminary notification issued in respect of the suit lands.

It is submitted that the claimants have let-in sufficient evidence in respect of the consent award having similarities and applicability to the acquired lands of the claimants, the Appellate Court has totally lost sight and awarded meager compensation of Rs.2,29,248/- per acre,
applying capitalization method.

5. Per contra, learned AAG appearing for the State, placing reliance on Ex.P5- another consent award, submits that for the lands situated in Kadaganchi village, which is 9 kilometers away from the acquired lands, the consent award determined is Rs.2,50,000/- per acre for the dry land.

The learned AAG submits that if Ex.P5 is taken base for consideration of awarding compensation to the claimants herein, the award of compensation by the Appellate Court is just and proper as the claimants/appellants were awarded Rs.2,29,248/- per acre, which warrants no interference by this Shivasharanappa S/O Hanamanthappa And ... vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer ... on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149334518/
3 Court.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:4669 6.

Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, the point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether the claimants/appellants have made out a case for enhancement of compensation by placing reliance on Ex.P4-the consent award?"
7.

The law is well settled that the consent award cannot form basis to award or decide compensation in another acquisition, the Apex Court in the case of Special Land Acquisition Officer and Others Vs.
N. Savitha1

entities.text:
Special Land Acquisition Officer and Others Vs.
N. Savitha1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: has observed that solely relying upon the consent award the compensation in another acquisition cannot be awarded.
The Apex Court observed that the consent award cannot be the basis to award and / or determine the compensation in other acquisition, more particularly, when there are other evidence on record.
8. Bearing in mind, the settled proposition of law, the material on record needs to be looked into.

Under 4(1) notification issued on 28.06.2007 the lands of the 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 316 NC:
2024:KHC-K:4669 claimants situated at Bommanahalli village, Kalaburagi District was acquired for the purpose of construction of irrigation tank.

9. Ex.P4-the consent award placed reliance by the claimants pertains to Nadisinnur, Firozabad and Kiranagi villages of Kalaburagi, the purpose of the acquisition is a thermal project under the notification dated 2009.
In the consent award, compensation of Rs.9,00,000/- per acre has been awarded.
In the case of a consent award, one is required to consider the circumstances under which the consent award was passed and the parties agreed to accept the compensation at a particular rate.

Claimant No.1 examined himself as PW.1, in his evidence, he stated that the land acquired is fertile black cotton soil, further, he stated that similar lands were acquired for a thermal power project during the same period and the award was passed on 08.07.2010 and the lands acquired in the said villages stated supra under the consent award and the lands in the present case have similar NC:
2024:KHC-K:4669 potentialities and fertility.
The claimants stated that they are entitled for the same compensation with appropriate depreciation from the preliminary notification.
The evidence of P.W.1 was also pertaining to Ex.P5, where another consent award has been passed and lands acquired therein were awarded compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- per acre for dry land.
P.W.1 spoke about the fertility of the acquired lands, categorically stated about the growing of crops during different seasons and also produced the price list and the yield certificate.
P.W.1 in his cross-examination deposed and admitted that the lands pertaining to the consent award Ex.P.4 and P.5 are situated at a distance of more than 15 km from the acquired land.

The cross-examination of P.W.1 reads as under:
"It is true one gunta of photo kharab land is also acquired.
It is true as per Ex.P.4 and 5 the consent awards pertaining to the lands situated at the distance of more than 15-Kms.
It is true I have not produced any document as to show the land acquired near Kadganchi as per ex.P.5 is situated adjacent to acquired land.

It is true the land Shivasharanappa S/O Hanamanthappa And ... vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer ... on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149334518/
4 acquired near Kadganchi village situated adjacent to Aland-Gulbarga road.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is false to suggest that, the NC: 2024:KHC-K:4669 land acquired in this case and also land acquired as per Ex.P.4 and 5 is no way concerned to the acquired land in this case.
The land acquired in this case is a fertile land and the land acquired at Kadganchi as per Ex.P.5 is a red stone soil land."

10. The claimants are seeking enhancement of compensation based on Ex.P.4-the consent award,
P.W.1 spoke about the fertility of the acquired land and the similarity of the lands acquired under the consent award.

The land acquired in the consent award is black soil, which is evident from Ex.P.4 and the acquired lands are also black soil in light of the evidence of P.W.1 and 4(1)
notification.
11. Ex.P.4 indicates the market value of the lands situated in the said villages, which is around Rs.36,764/- for Nadisinnur village, Rs.47,009.73/- for Firozabad and Rs.39,862.46/- for Kiranagi.

The lands acquired indicate the market value to be around Rs.37,358/- per acre under 4(1)
notification.

12. The Appellate Court, while passing the award of compensation, arrived at a conclusion that the consent - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4669 awards have been made under different sets of circumstances and that nothing has been placed on record by the claimants to show that the acquired lands are as fertile as the acquired lands in Ex.P4 and Ex.P5 - consent awards.
The Appellate Court fell in error and misdirected itself in holding that the consent awards were made under different sets of circumstances.

The claimants are not only placing reliance on the consent awards, but also on the other materials, more particularly the evidence of P.W.1, the similarity and potentiality of the lands acquired, which is black cotton soil, the Appellate Court has failed to consider the same.
13. Ex

another consent award placed reliance by AAG is pertaining to village Kadaganchi, which is around 9 kilometers away from the acquired lands, award of compensation is Rs.2,50,000/- per acre for the dry land.

If the average of compensation as awarded in Ex.P4 and Ex.P5 is calculated,
the market value that would be arrived at is Rs.5,75,000/-, the notification under Ex.P4 - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:4669 is of the year 2009 and in the instant case, the notification is dated 28.06.2007,
taking de-escalation of 5% per annum on Rs.5,75,000/-, the compensation that the claimants/ appellants would be entitled to is Rs.5,18,937/- per acre.

For the foregoing reasons, the points framed for consideration is answered in affirmative in favour of the claimants/appellants holding that the claimants/appellants are entitled for compensation of Rs.5,18,937/- per acre with all statutory benefits and interest thereon and accordingly, this Court pass the following:
Shivasharanappa S/O Hanamanthappa And ... vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer ...

on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149334518/
5 ORDER i.
The miscellaneous second appeal is allowed with cost.
ii. The claimants/appellants are entitled for compensation of Rs.5,18,937/- per acre as against Rs.2,29,248/- per acre with all statutory benefits and interest as per law.
iii. For the delay caused in preferring the appeal before the Appellate Court, the claimants/appellants are not entitled for the interest for the said period.
The deficit Court fee, if any, to be paid by the claimants/appellants within a period of eight weeks.
